eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **AI Act (GPAI Transparency Obligations):** Providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models must now publish detailed summaries of the content used for training and implement technical measures to prevent the generation of illegal content. Previously: No EU-wide transparency requirements for training data sets. Now: Mandatory public disclosure of training data summaries and documented copyright compliance for all models with systemic risk. Deadline: Immediate effect as of November 15, 2026. This increases compliance costs for AI developers and affects Portuguese tech startups exporting AI services to the EU. [Official Journal of the EU]

• **CSRD (Delegated Act on SME Reporting):** Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) listed on EU regulated markets must now adopt the simplified sustainability reporting standard (VSME). Previously: Listed SMEs were largely exempt or relied on voluntary, fragmented frameworks. Now: Mandatory reporting using the streamlined VSME standard for the 2026 reporting cycle (due 2027). This requires Portuguese SMEs listed on Euronext Lisbon to implement formal sustainability tracking systems immediately. [European Commission]

• **MiCA (Asset-Referenced Tokens Decision):** Issuers of asset-referenced tokens (stablecoins) are now required to maintain a reserve of assets that is legally segregated and held in custody by an independent third party. Previously: Variable national rules with no uniform EU reserve threshold or custody requirement. Now: Mandatory 1:1 reserve ratio with daily liquidity audits and strict segregation of assets from the issuer's own balance sheet. Deadline: Enforceable as of November 18, 2026. This reduces counterparty risk for Portuguese investors holding EU-regulated stablecoins. [EUR-Lex]

Why it matters: The EU has shifted from framework-setting to hard enforcement, specifically targeting the operational transparency of AI and the financial solvency of crypto-assets.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
No significant laws, decree-laws, or regulations with material impact on citizens or businesses were published in the Diário da República between November 14 and November 21, 2026.

Items in progress to watch:
- The approval and implementation of the 2027 State Budget (Orçamento do Estado 2027), specifically regarding adjustments to IRC (Corporate Tax) brackets and IRS (Personal Income Tax) thresholds.
- Pending regulatory updates to the "Simplex" administrative simplification program, intended to reduce licensing timelines for industrial and commercial investments.

Why it matters: The current legislative lull indicates a transition toward the finalization of the 2027 State Budget, which will be the primary driver of tax and investment policy for the next calendar year.
